fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Millennial Reign Doorway", "body": "Chance says what pulled him into Tartaria was the millennial reign theory, the claim that the Rapture already happened, that Jesus returned and reigned for a thousand years, and that we are now inside the little season of Revelation with Satan loosed again. He made a full episode on the provenance of Revelation, arguing it did not reach us in the same canonical package as the gospels and may have been composed centuries later, possibly as late as the Renaissance. Christian conspiracy circles, he says, use that timeline to explain 1700s and 1800s cathedrals as built during Jesus's reign."}, {"title": "A Genre With A Formula", "body": "What Tartaria really is, Chance argues, is a genre with a repeatable formula: show a photo of an 1800s building, claim the population was too small, the logistics impossible and the construction record missing, read a line off Wikipedia, project incredulity for twenty minutes and conclude it must be Tartaria. He tells Joel and Aurassimus that most of the big channels launched in 2025 and 2026 are full AI productions, and he screen shares a Tartaria Instagram post that had pasted the floating city from the video game BioShock Infinite over a Chicago World's Fair photograph."}, {"title": "Inside The Insane Asylums", "body": "Chance's favorite work in the project is on the 1800s insane asylums, the long batwing buildings that Tartaria videos call repurposed old world castles or extermination camps for people who remembered. Across roughly seven hours of content he presents construction records for ten or twelve of them, down to receipt books for the masons and the steam power, most of it pulled from archive.org and state legislature minutes. In Missouri, he found, lawmakers resisted building one until the governor took his own life. The design came from alienists and their philosophy of environmental determinism: fresh air, clean food, nature and space."}, {"title": "Chicago, The Fair And The Fire", "body": "Two load bearing pillars of the theory sit in Chicago. Chance says the World's Fair buildings were framed in wood and some steel, then molded in a plaster called staff to imitate carved stone, essentially a movie set, and that a surviving book of blueprints is named in Howdy McCoskey's own book after McCoskey claims none exist. He ballparks the cost at 600 to 800 million dollars in modern money. On the Great Chicago Fire he points to wooden sidewalks, tar coated wood block streets, one inch of rain from July to October, and fires across Wisconsin and Michigan the same day."}, {"title": "Donnelly, Atlantis And The Sacred Cow", "body": "Researching the fire led Chance to Ignatius Donnelly, whom he calls the modern origin of the whole lost civilization and cataclysm genre. In Ragnarok, written about twelve years after 1871, Donnelly blamed the Chicago and Peshtigo fires on fragments of Biela's Comet, which astronomers had watched split in two in 1846. Chance's objection is that the comet does not come around until late November while those fires burned in early October. Donnelly's Atlantis, he argues, seeded Blavatsky and Steiner, and he reads Plato's Atlantis as allegory: a traditionalist society and a progressive proto Athens destroying each other."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Chance Garton returns for his third visit to Here for the Truth, and his first in four years. Chance is a biofield tuning practitioner, host of the InnerVerse Podcast, and one of the rare researchers willing to take the Tartaria conspiracy seriously enough to check its claims against the primary sources. Once a believer himself, Chance traces how the “Old World reset” narrative of mud floods, buried cities, and buildings too beautiful for ordinary people to have built snowballed into a grand unifying theory that now operates like a religion inside truther culture. Underneath the debunking is the conversation that matters: how identity fuses with belief, why “they lied to us” becomes permission to believe anything, and what it costs to hand your discernment to a guru. A study in the one discipline every truth-seeker needs, the courage to hold no sacred cows.
